Declare the database

Source: R/io_data.R
declare_io.Rd

Builds the database used by the model from objects the user already has: the technical structure, gross output, final demand, the satellite accounts and, optionally, a corridor. The package never parses free-form spreadsheets and never searches a database for accounts or corridors: the user states what each object is. The vectors may be objects already in the R session; pass them by name.

Usage

declare_io(
  Z = NULL,
  x,
  f,
  E = NULL,
  D = NULL,
  A = NULL,
  B = NULL,
  corridor = NULL,
  floor = NULL,
  ceiling = NULL,
  sectors = NULL
)

Arguments

Z, A, B

Technical structure (n x n): give exactly one.

x

Gross output (n). Must be positive.

f

Final demand (n): the default economic goals.

E, D

Satellite accounts: give exactly one (see above).

corridor, floor, ceiling

Corridor (n, proportions alpha_h): give corridor, or floor and/or ceiling, or none (free).

sectors

Data frame with columns code and name (optional). Without it, codes come from the names of x, the column names of Z, or become S01, S02, ...

Value

Object of class lexio_io.

Details

Notation (Rocha, 2026, section 4.2): Z intermediate consumption, x gross output (VBP), f final demand, A = Z x^-1 technical coefficients, B = I - A, E_j level of a satellite account in sector j (toe, jobs, ...), D = E x^-1 direct impact coefficients (one row per account), alpha_h corridor of sector h.

  • Technical structure: exactly one of Z (flows, then A = Z / x by column), A or B.

  • Satellite accounts: exactly one of E (levels, then D = E / x) or D (coefficients). Each can be a named list of vectors (one per account), a data frame with one column per account, or a matrix (sectors x accounts for E; accounts x sectors for D, as in the notation above). The names are the account names.

  • Corridor (optional), a vector of proportions alpha_h (one per sector) that bounds the deviations of the economic goals: corridor = alpha bounds both sides, d_h^- <= alpha_h |g_h| and d_h^+ <= alpha_h |g_h|; floor = alpha bounds only d^- (G_h x >= g_h - alpha_h |g_h|); ceiling = alpha bounds only d^+ (G_h x <= g_h + alpha_h |g_h|). floor and ceiling can be given together, with different values. NA in a sector means no bound in that sector. With no corridor, the model is free (no bound on the economic deviations).

See also

read_io() to read the same database from a folder of CSV files or an .xlsx workbook, validate_io(), write_io().

Examples

Z <- matrix(c(3, 1, 2, 7), 2)          # Miller and Blair (2022), Example 13.7
x <- c(10, 10)
io <- declare_io(Z = Z, x = x, f = x - rowSums(Z),
                 D = list(OIL = c(0.2, 0.3), EMP = c(0.1, 0.2)))
io
#> <lexio_io> 2 sectors, 2 satellite account(s): OIL, EMP | declared as Z + D | corridor: free 
#>   base OIL = D x = 5.00
#>   base EMP = D x = 3.00
